Jordan — thanks for the signal and the logs. Really sorry you're seeing this. We're treating as P0.

Short answers up front:
1) We're seeing a sustained increase in queue depth on your reserved pool (same pool id: rp-us-west-3-01). Early telemetry points to a sudden qps burst and an unexpected large request (20k token batch) from a subset of sessions that caused KV-cache churn.
2) Immediate mitigation options we can do in the next 20–30 minutes:
   - Switch your routing to a higher-throughput instance family (burst for 1 hour) — requires exec approval for temporary capacity change.
   - Enable per-customer hard throttles for long requests (we can cut CRM-facing requests >10k tokens).
   - Turn on aggressive prefix cache for your auth route (low risk).

I'll loop our infra lead David for a quick root-cause pull and to stand up a temporary routing change if we get approval. Naomi, Marissa — marking this as priority for the customer SLA/credits conversation and external comms. Jordan — I'll confirm ETA in the next 15 minutes.

Quick technical readout from infra:

What we see
- RP pool rp-us-west-3-01 experienced a concentrated hotset: 4 clients issued a few very long sequences at 07:42–07:46 (one request ~19.8k tokens).
- KV cache eviction rates spiked, causing a collapse in effective cache hit ratio from ~94% to ~47% for ~18 minutes. That increased per-token work and led to queueing/backpressure -> tail 5xx.
- Observed qps bump: baseline 450 qps -> transient 1,900 qps (burst window).

Immediate actions taken (10:00–11:00):
- Applied emergency per-session token cap (10k) to reduce new long-run requests (non-invasive).
- Cast an emergency route to a burst node family (n4-highmem-burst) for 30 minutes; that reduced p95 latency to ~420ms and 5xx to <1% for the trial segment.
- Collected artifacts: qps chart (attached) and an LRU snapshot (kv-cache-dump-velvetpay-20260520.txt).

Proposal / ask
- To fully remediate we recommend: authorize a 6-hour burst of reserved capacity while we patch the customer workload and tune caching. Long-term fixes: define a max-token SLA, and patch our prefix-caching heuristics for their access pattern.
- Operationally this requires a quick exec approval for a temporary reserved top-up (billing impact noted below).

Billing note (for planning)
- 1-hour burst estimate: $Xk (we will provide exact figures to Finance).

Attachments: qps-metrics-velvetpay-20260520.png, kv-cache-dump-velvetpay-20260520.txt
